There are no colleges, no guilds, no lineages in the formal sense; master-shamans take one to three apprentices over a five-to-ten-year horseback apprenticeship; identification is by the hearing-gift, a phonological capacity detectable in childhood. Qollari produces cinchona bark — the primary high-altitude pharmacological export — and the Basin's four port zones consume, trans-ship, and reinsure virtually the entire Qollari export volume. The ancestor-smith tiers — Nokul (initiate), Amori (master), Lapam (ancestor) — are temporal coordinates. A tier promotion closes one generation and opens another; the date is inscribed in the forge-temple's click-register ledger, the only written calendar the Ngaru-Bon maintain. The Outside-Forge Network uses the same tier names but refuses the Inner Council's promotion authority.

entities.lede: The Kheshkai political economy is built on Varkosh oaths underwritten by herd wealth. Every pasture-rotation assignment, marriage-alliance commitment, and protection-rent obligation assumes that the animals producing the wool, the felt, the horse-geldings, and the meat will survive the winter. The Oral-Memory Council's doctrine acknowledges one exception: a dzud — the summer-drought-plus-deep-snow winter that kills herds in place — voids the oaths that the herds underwrite.

entities.lede: Tegu Bokh's doctrine is simple: ONE sky = ONE correct liturgy. This would collapse the polyvocal seasonal-oath practice — in which different clans, different master-shamans, and different herder-mothers may observe slightly different festival timings based on local grass conditions — into a fixed calendar of correct liturgical moments. It would be the first written-and-codified Kheshkai calendar. The Oral-Memory Council's entire authority rests on polyvocality. The Council does not consult archives when two speakers disagree on what was ruled in a given year.

entities.lede: The Oravan calendar is performed, not computed. Each priestess-queen declares the monsoon-window opening from her own polity's cyclone-shoulder observation, and no central council resolves inter-island disputes. Workshop pluralism — three to seven senior workshops per polity, each with divergent phonetic and observational traditions — means that two priestess-queens on different islands may observe the same cyclone shoulder two weeks apart and produce incompatible calendars. Both observations are theologically valid. Both priestess-queens are in their dual-aspect register.

Together they constitute the Kheshkai's continental commercial footprint, denominated in Khazadari rate-schedule terms by the Basin-facing commercial factors the Khazadari guild trains.

The flood-grain economy runs across two institutional tiers.
